newsitem.title: UK: Rolls-Royce shares up as dividend raised.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce shares up as dividend raised.

text.p: Shares in engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce Plc were higher on Thursday, after the company raised its annual dividend and said it was currently negotiating the sale of its steam engine businesses. The shares were up 5p at 244p by 0917 GMT. The company had reported a pretax loss of 28 million stg after profits were wiped out by 263 million stg in provisions, write-offs and losses as a result of the group's decision to withdraw from steam power generation market.
But analysts said the charges were already known and the underlying performance of the group was slightly ahead of expectations.
"They were a good set of results, slightly better than people's expectations," said Paul Pickford, industry analyst at Panmure Gordon.
Rolls-Royce raised its total dividend to 5.3 pence compared with 5.0 pence in 1995.
"It was good to see a resumption in dividend growth, which we haven't seen since 1992," Pickford commented.

"But the main feature everyone was looking for was news on the disposal of the International Combustion and Parsons steam businesses," said the analyst. "They are in negotiations at the moment and that was very positive."
The company said it was close to selling both of its steam power businesses and expects to make announcements in the next few weeks.
Operating profits from the core aero-engines and industrial power businesses rose to 242 million stg from 178 million a year ago. --Elaine Hardcastle,London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
